Hi Ellen / Marco — great to hear you're seeing the latency and cost wins. I've attached the short PoC report with the perf tables and a simple cost model (helix-poc-performance-20270520.pdf). High level:
- Baseline (current infra equivalent): $0.016/token average unit cost
- Redwood hosted (no commit): $0.012/token @ current profile
- Estimated with 6-month reserved capacity (Dedicated): $0.009/token at 5k RTK sustained

I've also included a proposed commit worksheet (proposed-commit-model.xlsx) that shows tiered discounts at different throughput bands and a sample 12-month cadence with burst credits.

1) Ben can do a cost-run with your actual monthly token export to show a tailored forecast.
2) Laura can outline success metrics we'd include in the renewal (uptime, tail-latency SLO, cost per 1k tokens).
3) We can run a 30-day reserved trial on Dedicated for a smaller pool to validate latency at scale.

Available for a sync on Monday.

—Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa. A couple quick clarifying Qs:
- Our peak inference pattern is short bursts tied to customer campaigns (10-15M tokens/day peaks) with a much lower base. How would burst credits apply?
- Does KV/prefix caching from Redwood help our prompt-heavy retrieval flows?

If Ben or Laura can include those assumptions in the model that would be helpful. Ellen and I are trying to build a business case to take to procurement.

—Marco

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@helixai.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@helixai.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC wrap & next steps

Marco — quick answers inline.
- Bursts: Recommend Reserved + burst credits lane. Proposed commit sheet models a 20% headroom for burst with additional one-time burst credit buckets that amortize over the term. That lets you keep base commit low and absorb campaign spikes.
- Caching: Yes — prefix + KV caching is effective for retrieval-heavy prompts; we saw a 30–50% token reduction on repeated contexts in the PoC. For campaign bursts, this is biggest lever to reduce incremental spend.

I've attached a scenario sheet (in the same workbook) with a 1x/5x/10x run using Helix's token export we pulled from your staging. TL;DR: with a 12-month commit at 5k RTK sustained, your per-token goes to ~$0.0085 when amortized with burst credits; with a conservative 10x growth scenario the blended effective rate is ~$0.0102.

If you want, we can produce an ops runbook showing autoscaling thresholds and pre-warming triggers to keep p99 latency under your SLO during bursts.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ellen — thanks for the ask. Quick plan:
- Data residency: For Hosted, we keep inference telemetry and aggregate metrics in Redwood's telemetry store; no customer PII or payload text is persisted unless configured. For Dedicated (VPC), customer data remains inside the VPC with optional customer-managed KMS. I'll have a short 1-page data flow and a redlines-safe clause for your procurement team by EOD Friday.
- SLA & escalation: We'll provide sample SLA language (uptime, p50/p90/p99 latencies, MTTR) and a mapped escalation ladder (Support -> CSM -> Infra on-call -> VP Eng) with contact SLAs for Dedicated.
- Pricing: Vanessa will share a price-locked 12-month proposal by Monday. We'll include a 30-day validation window on reserved capacity and a 15% intro discount on the first quarter for the initial commit size outlined in Ben's sheet.

Action items assigned: Vanessa to finalize proposal; Ben to produce ops runbook summary; Laura to draft success metrics for renewal; Vivek to deliver data/SLA artifacts and legal-safe language.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
